first.rationale:
Two of the three current problems are funnel-mechanics problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and the inherited record contains two apparently convergent findings on that exact lever: memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup field reduction produced a durable SMB activation lift). That convergence, plus direct alignment with the declining metrics, makes simplify_onboarding the best single-slot bet for sustainable qualified revenue. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing (memory_73) despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 reports acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about retention or downstream account quality, and discount-led acquisition into a price-sensitive segment is the classic way to book short-term revenue that fails the 'sustainable, qualified' test. It also concedes the price frame to the competitor rather than repairing the funnel we control.

I am spending the single verification pull on memory_86 rather than on my rejected alternative, because memory_86 carries the load-bearing weight of my decision and its apparent corroboration by memory_31 may be illusory. Both are consolidated summaries from archived sources; if they trace to the same underlying experiment, I have one data point wearing two hats, not independent replication. I also want to know what memory_86's original record actually measured: 'completion rates and time-to-value' and 'early product adoption' are proxy metrics, not qualified revenue. A lift in completion is compatible with simply pushing lower-intent accounts further down the funnel.

Downstream value risk: shortening onboarding and cutting fields removes exactly the qualification signal that memory_44's sales-assisted enterprise path depends on. A change tuned for SMB self-serve throughput can quietly degrade enterprise pipeline quality, and that harm would surface in a later quarter, after the experiment is scored a success. So the experiment must be segmented — apply to self-serve/SMB, hold the enterprise demo-request path intact — and must be read on qualified-revenue and retention endpoints, not completion rate alone.

Standard experiment scale with holdout, not broad rollout: the supporting memories are 15-64 days old, predate the competitor's move, and the current declines may share a cause (a platform or funnel regression) that a shortened form would mask rather than fix. If verification shows memory_86 and memory_31 are the same source, or that neither tracked revenue, I will drop to a small guarded test and treat activation_messaging (memory_91) as the fallback, since it addresses the activation decline without touching qualification data.

final.rationale:
Verification strengthened the case. exp_86 was not a proxy-only result: alongside completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days it carried 30-day retention +3%, so the shortened flow moved a durability metric rather than merely pushing low-intent accounts further down the funnel. That was my main worry and it is substantially reduced. Committing to simplify_onboarding.

What verification did NOT resolve, and I am not going to paper over: (1) I still cannot tell whether memory_31 is independent of memory_86 or a second summary of overlapping work, so I am treating this as one well-evidenced finding, not two converging ones, and sizing accordingly. (2) 30-day retention is a good signal but it is not qualified revenue over a meaningful horizon; the primary objective is long-term qualified revenue and exp_86 does not directly speak to it. (3) exp_86 predates the competitor's entry pricing. A funnel improvement measured in a calmer market may behave differently when price-sensitive SMBs now have a cheap alternative one click away — faster onboarding may simply deliver them to a comparison they lose. (4) The current -4%/-6% declines may share an upstream cause; a shorter form could mask a regression rather than fix it, so I want instrumentation on where accounts are actually dropping, not just the aggregate completion number.

Downstream value risk stands and drives the design. Cutting required fields removes the qualification signal that the enterprise sales-assisted path (memory_44) runs on, and that damage would land in a later quarter after this experiment has already been scored a win. Therefore: apply to the self-serve/SMB segment only, leave the enterprise demo-request path fully intact, and keep a holdout. Read the result on qualified revenue and retention as primary endpoints with completion as a diagnostic — explicitly not the reverse — and hold enterprise pipeline quality as a guardrail metric that can fail the test even if SMB numbers look good.

Standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the evidence is now good enough to justify a real read with a holdout, but it is one confirmed record from day 52 in a changed competitive market, and rolling broadly would forfeit the ability to detect the enterprise-side harm before it compounds. I am still declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor pressure — memory_73 reports acquisition and revenue lift but is silent on retention and account quality, which is exactly the shape of a finding that buys short-term revenue against the sustainability objective. Activation_messaging (memory_91) remains the fallback if the enterprise guardrail trips.
